investigationQuestions.question_text: Can the bank provide transaction-level authentication records showing the authentication method, timestamps, device or wallet identifiers, and evidence of physical or digital card presentation for all disputed transactions following the new digital token registration?

Can the bank provide records showing any fraud monitoring alerts, anomaly detection notifications, or transaction velocity checks triggered by the disputed transactions, including the exact timing of these alerts relative to the customer's fraud hotline notification and subsequent containment actions?

evidenceRequests.request_text: Please provide transaction-level authentication records including the authentication method used, timestamps, device or wallet identifiers, and any evidence of physical or digital card presentation for all disputed transactions after the new digital token was registered.

Please provide bank records of any fraud monitoring alerts, anomaly detection notifications, and transaction velocity checks triggered by the disputed transactions, including exact timestamps of these alerts and any related fraud containment actions taken.
Please provide the customer's fraud hotline call log or call recording that shows the date and time the fraud was first reported to the bank.

executive_summary.text: This case pack summarises 2 investigation themes identified from the case record: Authentication Chain and Digital Token Registration, Customer Notification and Fraud Containment Actions. The pack sets out the bank assertions, material findings, outstanding evidence requests, and relevant regulatory references associated with each theme. It does not determine liability or make legal conclusions.

key_themes.theme_title: Authentication Chain and Digital Token Registration
key_themes.theme_summary: This theme consolidates assertions and findings related to the customer's authentication method, focusing on the new digital token registration before disputed transactions and the implications for 3D Secure and contactless transaction authentication.
key_themes.issue: Whether transaction-level authentication records demonstrate legitimate customer authorisation after the registration of a new digital token and proper device or wallet presentation for disputed transactions.

regulatory_references.clause_title: FSM-N13 – FI Duty: Protect Customer Information from Unauthorised Access
regulatory_references.clause_summary:
9. A relevant entity must implement IT controls to protect customer information from 
   unauthorised access or disclosure.

A relevant entity must ensure that multi-factor authentication is implemented for:
(a) all administrative accounts in respect of any operating system, database, application, 
    security appliance or network device that is a critical system; and
(b) all accounts on any system used by the relevant entity to access customer information 
    through the internet.

key_themes.theme_title: Customer Notification and Fraud Containment Actions
key_themes.theme_summary: This theme groups the customer's fraud hotline notification and the bank's subsequent containment actions, including requests for records and logs of these interactions and any fraud detection alerts triggered by the disputed transactions.
key_themes.issue: Whether fraud monitoring systems triggered alerts or flagged anomalies in response to the velocity and pattern of the disputed transactions and the timeline of the customer’s fraud hotline notification.

   or such longer period as the Authority may allow, from the discovery of the relevant incident. 
   The report must contain—
       (a) an executive summary of the relevant incident;

       (c) a description of the impact of the relevant incident on the relevant entity’s—

‘customer’, in relation to a relevant entity, includes:
(a) the Monetary Authority of Singapore;
(b) any monetary authority or central bank of any other country or territory; and
(c) any company which carries on a banking business, a merchant banking business,
    or an investment banking business.

regulatory_references.clause_title: FSM-N13 – FI Duty: Notify MAS Within 1 Hour of Relevant Incident
regulatory_references.clause_summary:
7. A relevant entity must notify the Authority as soon as possible, but not later than 1 hour, upon 
   the discovery of a relevant incident.
